# Import Meter Data

FLOWCAL has the ability to import gas or liquid meter data using a <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCTextPopup MCTextPopupHotSpot MCTextPopup_Open glossaryTerm MCTextPopupHotSpot_" alt="Closed" data-mc-alt2="Open">CFX file<span class="MCTextPopupBody popupBody"><span class="MCTextPopupArrow"></span>A proprietary binary file format used to bring meter flow data and configuration information into FLOWCAL.</span></a>. A flow computer or SCADA system will generate a CFX file that can contain meter flow history, meter configuration, events, alarms, product information and/or analysis data. This data is brought into FLOWCAL for calculation and balancing purposes. The data can be validated on import to see if there are any discrepancies and/or exceptions on the imported data.

<div class="procedure">

To manually import a file:

1.  Go to **Import** \> **Meter Data**.

2.  Choose a meter, location or list to import data into.

3.  If you choose a list or location, you can select **Use Start Date** and enter a starting date for data. This filters out data recorded prior to the selected time.

    By default, FLOWCAL only imports the last 35 days of data it finds for each meter. When importing for a single meter, you can preview the data in the Volume Editor before saving any data. When importing by list or location, all meters in the list or location will be imported. You will then need to review data in the Volume Editor and purge or edit any incorrect data.

4.  Click the browse button beside the **Folder or File Name** field to select the CFX file, or type the file path into the field.

5.  **Optional:** Select a driver (typically STNDCFX). If the meter has already been set up in the Meter Editor with the correct import path and import driver, this is not necessary.

6.  Click the **Import** button.

7.  When the Volume Editor displays, review the data to make sure it has imported correctly.

8.  Go to **Data** \> **Save** and close the Volume Editor.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 488;height: 236;" />

</div>

Windows has a hard-coded limit of 260 characters for file paths; file paths longer than this will not work. Importing files from a local install allows for using drive letters for network file paths; however, Citrix resolves the actual network location, which can cause the number of characters in a file path to exceed this limit.
